title: Repair delivery without weakening identity or encryption
description: Inject a failure, choose a recovery contract, and change the retry count. The topology shows where progress stops and whether recovery creates duplicates, misses a device, or breaks the privacy boundary.

stages.label: Sender device
stages.role: Creates one logical message ID and encrypts separately for recipient devices.

stages.label: Encrypted ingest
stages.role: Authenticates the command and accepts ciphertext without possessing content keys.

stages.label: Per-device queues
stages.role: Tracks independent delivery state for phone, tablet, web, and desktop sessions.

stages.label: Recipient device
stages.role: Authenticates, decrypts, persists locally, and suppresses an already-seen message ID.

stages.label: Device acknowledgement
stages.role: Removes only that device's queue item; read state remains a separate event.

scenarios.label: Acknowledgement is lost
scenarios.detail: The recipient persists the message, but its delivery ACK never reaches the service.
scenarios.event: The service cannot tell whether the final network hop failed or the ACK was lost after persistence.
scenarios.userImpact: A retry is required, but it must not create another visible bubble.
scenarios.retryBehavior: Retry the same device queue item with the same logical message ID after bounded backoff.
scenarios.dedupeBehavior: The recipient checks its durable seen-ID set before display and ACKs an already-seen retry.
scenarios.queueBehavior: Only the unacknowledged device retains work; other device queues stay complete.
scenarios.keyBehavior: The existing authenticated session remains valid, so no key repair is needed.
recovery: Retry the ciphertext envelope with the original message ID.
Suppress the repeated display on the recipient device.
Record the device ACK and remove only that queue item.

scenarios.label: One recipient device is offline
scenarios.detail: The tablet receives the message while the phone remains disconnected.
scenarios.event: A user-level success signal is ambiguous because one device completed and another still has no copy.
scenarios.userImpact: The phone should catch up after reconnect without redelivering a second copy to the tablet.
scenarios.retryBehavior: Retry only the phone's pending queue when its session reconnects.
scenarios.dedupeBehavior: Each device suppresses retries against its own durable seen-ID set.
scenarios.queueBehavior: Phone and tablet delivery records advance independently under one logical message ID.
scenarios.keyBehavior: Each device uses its own encrypted envelope and session state.
recovery: Keep the phone queue item after the tablet ACK arrives.
Bind the reconnect to the phone's device identity and cursor.
Deliver and ACK the phone envelope without reopening the tablet queue.

scenarios.label: Encryption session is stale
scenarios.detail: The recipient reinstalled the app, so a queued envelope targets an obsolete device session.
scenarios.event: Routing succeeds, but the recipient cannot authenticate or decrypt ciphertext created for the old session.
scenarios.userImpact: Delivery pauses for that device while clients establish a fresh authenticated session.
scenarios.retryBehavior: Do not repeat the same undecryptable bytes indefinitely; classify the failure and repair the session.
scenarios.dedupeBehavior: Preserve the logical message ID when the sender creates a replacement envelope for the new session.
scenarios.queueBehavior: Other device queues continue; only the stale device envelope is blocked.
scenarios.keyBehavior: Fetch the current device key bundle, establish a new session on the sender, and encrypt again client-side.
recovery: Mark the obsolete session envelope as requiring key repair.
Fetch and verify the recipient device's current key bundle.
Re-encrypt on the sender under the same logical message ID, then resume that device queue.

scenarios.label: New-device keys are unavailable
scenarios.detail: The sender cannot establish an authenticated session for a newly linked recipient device.
scenarios.event: The privacy boundary blocks envelope creation before the server can accept a deliverable payload.
scenarios.userImpact: That device waits for key material; the system must not silently downgrade to plaintext.
scenarios.retryBehavior: Back off key-bundle fetches separately from ciphertext delivery retries.
scenarios.dedupeBehavior: Once encryption succeeds, enqueue one envelope under the original logical message ID.
scenarios.queueBehavior: Existing recipient devices can proceed while the new device remains pending key setup.
scenarios.keyBehavior: Replenish and verify signed prekeys, then let the sender establish the session and encrypt locally.
recovery: Expose a key-setup delay instead of claiming delivery.
Replenish and verify the recipient device's signed key material.
Create ciphertext on the sender and start the new device queue only after verification.

policies.label: Bounded per-device recovery
policies.detail: Reuse the logical ID, retain independent device queues, and repair key sessions at the clients.

policies.label: Retry as a new message
policies.detail: Create a new message ID for every uncertain attempt.

policies.label: First device ACK completes the user
policies.detail: Keep one user-level queue and drop blocked device envelopes.

policies.label: Server plaintext fallback
policies.detail: Ask the service to bypass a failed key session by delivering readable content.
